item.title: Attosecond streaking of photoelectron angular momentum
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 24 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02020-z Angle-resolved attosecond streaking measurements are performed on helium and neon to probe the evolution of continuum-electron partial waves during continuum–continuum transitions, and uncover the angular momentum of continuum-electron peaks at the crest of the electric field.

item.title: Volumetrically continuous 3D dynamic holography via cascaded light-field propagation
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02016-9 Cascaded light-field propagation enhances three-dimensional holography by transforming crosstalk into constructive signals. Using an untrained neural framework, the method achieves continuous projections along with improvements in contrast and spatial resolution without extensive computational demands.

item.title: Millimetre-wave generation with 18 zs Hz<sup>−1/2</sup> timing noise floor via Kerr optical frequency division
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02014-x Low-noise millimetre-waves are generated by injection-locking a Kerr microcomb to a dual-wavelength Brillouin laser, which serves as the optical reference. A timing noise floor of 18 zs Hz−1/2 is achieved. The integrated timing jitter is 135 as from 1 kHz to 1 MHz.

item.description: arXiv:2609.29415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical Kerr nonlinearity is central to optical bistability in high-Q microcavities. item.title: Inverted phosphorescent OLEDs with plasmon coupling from quantum dot interlayers for enhanced efficiency
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 15 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02001-2 The introduction of a layer of quantum dots reduces plasmonic losses in organic light-emitting diodes.

item.title: Graphene measurements reveal energy-loss and quantum-coherence exponents diverge under gate control
item.description: Scientists have shown that the two exponents (inelastic scattering exponent and dephasing exponent) commonly used to describe electron scattering in graphene do not necessarily follow the same behavior. Using gated epitaxial graphene, a multi-institutional team of researchers independently extracted the two exponents through current-heating measurements and weak-localization analysis. item.title: Physicists crack the math connecting ultraslow quantum magnetism to ultrafast black-hole physics
item.description: A team led by University at Buffalo physicists has found a mathematical solution that shows how a frustrated quantum magnet can transition from ultraslow behavior to ultrafast, highly entangled behavior resembling that of a black hole.

item.title: Photonic Legos of functional 3D thin-films unlock high-performance heterogeneous photonic integration
item.description: Photonic integrated circuits route information with optical signals instead of relying only on electrical currents. Silicon (Si) and silicon nitride (SiNx) are excellent photonic platforms for waveguides, but they cannot efficiently perform the ever-increasing tasks required for fully integrated optical systems. A heterogeneous photonic integration platform capable of interfacing different optical materials with high performance is thus an ongoing challenge for both academia and industry.

item.title: Physicists extend the search for quantum black holes at the LHC
item.description: Physicists at UC Santa Barbara have extended the search for evidence of microscopic black holes produced at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN). The formation of these tiny, fleeting objects at the LHC represents one way theorists have sought to resolve anomalies in our understanding of the basic structure of spacetime, while the method used to look for them demonstrates a new way of searching for new particles.

item.title: Observation of multiphoton entanglement in resonance fluorescence
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 24 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02022-x Multiphoton scattering process is extracted from the resonance fluorescence of a single 87Rb atom. Tripartite entanglement between the photons is verified by a violation of Svetlichny’s inequality. A quantum secret sharing protocol is demonstrated as an application example.
